 Shri Sameer Anant Athawale - Advocate for the appellan
 Shri Mahesh Kumar Sharma - Advocate for respondent No.
 Insurance Company.

Order 
This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 29/01/2016 passed by II Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Link Court, Alot, District Ratlam (M.P.) in Claim Case No.33/2014, whereby an amount of Rs.6,49,200/- has been awarded from the date of filing of claim petition the appellants / claimants /
survivors of the deceased Badrilal with interest @ 6% per annum, who died in a road traffic accident occurred on 12/07/2014.
2.

entities.text: II Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Link Court, Alot, District Ratlam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellants / survivors of the deceased submits that the learned Claims Tribunal has erred in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.4,000/- per month only.
At the time of accident deceased was working as Labourer and was doing agriculture work and was earning Rs.4,00,000/- per month.

His contention is that in case the income of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8416 2 MA-1819-2016 deceased is not proved by any cogent evidence,
income ought to have been assessed on the basis of circular issued by Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh under the Minimum Wages Act, according to which income of the deceased on the date of accident comes to Rs.5,975/- per month considering him as 'Semi Skilled'.

entities.text: Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 2.1 He further submits that the learned Claims Tribunal has awarded a meager amount of Rs.1,00,000/- in the head of Loss of Consortium and love and affection.

His contention is that all the survivors should have been awarded Rs.40,000/- each in the head of Loss of Consortium in the light of para 59.8 of the judgment delivered in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs.
Pranay Sethi & Ors. reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 . Learned Claims Tribunal has also not awarded any amount in head of Loss of Estate, therefore, an amount of Rs.15,000/- is to be added in this head in the light of aforesaid judgment.

entities.text:
National Insurance Company Limited Vs.
Pranay Sethi & Ors. reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

1 2.2 Learned counsel further submits that learned Claims Tribunal has erred in not awarding any amount in the head of future prospects, whereas as per para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (Supra) , looking to the age 42 years of the deceased, 25% amount is to be added in the head of Future Prospects.

Similarly, instead of adopting multiplier of 13, in the light of para 42 of the judgment in the case of Smt. Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 and followed in the case of Pranay Sethi (Supra), looking to the age of deceased, multiplier of 14 ought to have been applied.

entities.text: Smt. Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On these contentions, learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8416 3 MA-1819-2016 3.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that evidence led before the learned Claims Tribunal has been rightly appreciated.
The amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.
All the factors have been considered by the learned Claims Tribunal while awarding the compensation amount and no fault can be found with in the impugned award.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal being devoid of any substance.

4. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.

From perusal of the record, it is apparent that at the time of accident i.e. on 12/07/2014 deceased was working as labourer and agriculturist also, however, his income has not been established by adducing cogent evidence, therefore, in the light of the judgment delivered by the apex Court in the case o f Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr.

Vs . Mukesh Kumar Yadav reported in (2022) 1 SCC 198 : 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3093 , income of the deceased is to be assessed on the basis of circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act, therefore, on the basis of circular income of the deceased is assessed at Rs.5,975/- per month considering him as semi skilled.
6. Learned Claims Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.25,000/- in the head of Funeral Expenses, which according to 59.8 of the judgment in the case of Pranay Sethi (Supra) is on higher side
, therefore, the same is reduced from Rs.25,000/- to Rs.15,000/-.

However, since no amount has been awarded in the head of Loss of Estate, therefore, an amount of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:8416 4 MA-1819-2016 Rs.15,000/- is added in this head.
Since the survivors are wife, son, daughter and parents, which are seven in number, therefore, they all are entitled for an amount of Rs.40,000/- each in the head of loss of consortium.

7. Deceased was 42 years of age at the time of accident, therefore, as per para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (Supra) , 25% amount is added in the head of Future Prospects and similarly, looking to the age of the deceased, instead of 13, multiplier of 14 is adopted.
8.

Accordingly, the just and proper compensation amount comes as under:
Rs.5,975/- pm + 25% FP Ratanbai vs Meghsingh@Mahendra Singh on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185554293/
2 - 1/5th Personal Expenses Loss of Dependency:
X 12 Months X Multiplier of 14 = Rs.10,03,800/-
 Loss of Consortium: Rs.2,80,000/-
 Loss of Estate: Rs.15,000/-
 Funeral Expenses: Rs.15,000/-
 Total: Rs.13,13,800/-
 MACT
Awarded: Rs.6,49,200/-

Enhanced Amount: Rs.6,64,600/-
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.13,13,800/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.6,49,200/-.

Accordingly,
the appellants are entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.6,64,600/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.

9. Since the appeal has been valued at Rs.4,00,000/- only, therefore, the appellants are directed to pay additional court fees on the rest of the amount of Rs.2,64,600/- within a period of 30 days from today at the prevailing slab of court fees, thereafter, the same will be disbursed to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8416 5 MA-1819-2016 appellants.
Other terms and conditions of the impugned award including rate of interest @ 6% shall remain intact.
10. Subject to payment of requisite additional court fees within the aforesaid period, the enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate.

It is made clear, in case the court fees is not paid within the stipulated period, the appellants will not be entitled for claiming interest on the enhanced amount beyond 30 days' period, till the payment of requisite court fees.
11. Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellants / claimants is allowed to the extent as indicated hereinabove.
